title: NRI Investments Surge Into GIFT City as Edelweiss Launches India's First Multi-Manager Fund
excerpt: Fund commitments at India's international financial hub nearly doubled to $15.74 billion, with retail investor participation tripling as new products simplify cross-border investing for overseas Indians.
body:
• GIFT City fund commitments surged 87% year-on-year to $15.74 billion by March 2025, with retail investor participation nearly tripling in Q4 FY26
  • Edelweiss Mutual Fund launched India's first multi-manager equity fund from GIFT City, offering NRIs and OCIs diversified India exposure through a single $150,000 minimum investment
  • The fund follows an open-architecture model across eight schemes from top AMCs, with 60% flexicap and 40% midcap allocation — no single AMC exceeds 25-30% of the portfolio
  • Regulatory tailwinds including SEBI's removal of NRI investment caps and IFSCA's approval of the first Foreign Family Investment Fund are accelerating institutional interest

Gujarat's GIFT City is rapidly emerging as the preferred gateway for overseas Indians looking to invest in the country's equity markets, with fund commitments nearly doubling and a wave of new product launches designed to simplify what has long been a cumbersome process.

Edelweiss Mutual Fund has become the first asset management company to launch a multi-manager equity fund from GIFT City, targeting non-resident Indians and overseas citizens of India with a minimum ticket size of $150,000. The fund follows an open-architecture model — unlike conventional offerings tied to a single asset manager, it draws from schemes across India's top AMCs.

"We are very bullish on Gift City as a platform, and this multi-manager fund is the first of several funds we will launch. The fund is targeted at NRIs, OCIs, or anyone looking to get exposure to India."

— Radhika Gupta, MD & CEO, Edelweiss Mutual Fund

How the Fund Works

The Edelweiss multi-manager fund allocates 60% to flexicap strategies and 40% to midcap, giving investors roughly 40% large-cap exposure and 50-60% mid- and small-cap exposure overall. Fund selection follows a rigorous process: only the top 15 AMCs by equity assets under management qualify, and schemes must have a minimum 10-year track record.

https://x.com/ndtv/status/2091198138526933293

Scoring combines quantitative metrics — three- and five-year trailing and rolling returns, percentile rankings, Sharpe and information ratios — with qualitative AMC assessments, weighted 70-30. To prevent concentration, Edelweiss's own schemes are capped at 25-30% of the portfolio, with the same limit applying to any single AMC.

"Gift City fills a clear gap by offering investors quality Indian equity exposure with a dollar investment while avoiding the heavy paperwork that normally comes with such investments," Gupta told Mint. Onboarding takes four to five business days, with a fully digital option available through the KFintech platform.

The Bigger Picture: GIFT City's Rapid Growth

The Edelweiss launch is part of a broader surge in GIFT City's fund management ecosystem. Data from the International Financial Services Centres Authority shows total fund commitments jumped 87% year-on-year to $15.74 billion by March 2025, up from $8.41 billion a year earlier. Funds based in the IFSC had invested $8.08 billion across categories by that point.

Retail participation has accelerated sharply. The number of investors in retail schemes rose 177.5% quarter-on-quarter to 3,438 by March 2026, up from just 255 in September 2025 — a jump of nearly 1,250% in six months, according to IFSCA's latest bulletin. Total investors across all fund schemes reached 9,594.

"Most of the Q4 acceleration looks NRI-driven to me," said Amish Kapadia, founder of NRI Money Matters. "Three things converged: cross-border taxation discussions pushed money-routing questions to the forefront, the rupee trading near historic lows made dollar-denominated assets more tangible, and onboarding channels improved significantly."

Regulatory Tailwinds

Several policy changes have cleared the path. SEBI relaxed the 50% foreign investment requirement for GIFT City entities, allowing NRI and OCI investments to reach 100% of a fund — up from a structure that previously forced AMCs to maintain a 50-50 balance between foreign and NRI capital. In April 2026, IFSCA approved the first Foreign Family Investment Fund under its 2025 regulations, validating GIFT City as a jurisdiction for family offices and cross-border wealth structures.

The number of Fund Management Entities operating in the IFSC grew to 217 in the March 2026 quarter, up from 202 in the previous quarter, while registered schemes rose to 360 from 327.

What It Means for NRIs

For overseas Indians, GIFT City addresses several persistent pain points. Investments are denominated in US dollars, eliminating currency conversion friction. There is no tax deduction at source. And the KYC requirements align with global practices rather than India's domestic norms — a passport and address proof suffice, with verification by overseas professionals like lawyers or bankers.

Marcellus Investment Managers, which launched its GIFT City fund in early 2025, has seen its PMS offering there double in assets under management within a year. Mirae Asset manages approximately $40 million from around 200 NRI investors through its inbound AIF, primarily from the UAE, and has launched an outbound global allocation fund that raised $20 million in its first three months.

"GIFT City is fast becoming a compelling jurisdiction for both inbound investments from foreign and NRI investors, and outbound allocations by Indian residents — driven by regulatory clarity and tax incentives," said Pramod Gubbi, co-founder at Marcellus.

Whether the momentum holds will depend on continued regulatory support and whether the ecosystem can scale to match established hubs like Singapore and Dubai. But for NRIs seeking simplified, tax-efficient access to Indian equities, GIFT City is increasingly the answer.
